newsitem.title: USA: Icahn group loses court ruling in Marvel fight.
newsitem.headline: Icahn group loses court ruling in Marvel fight.

text.p: Carl Icahn Monday lost a round in court in his fight for Marvel Entertainment Group Inc. Monday when a federal judge blocked a group led by the financier from taking control of the comic book publisher.

A U.S. Bankruptcy Court judge granted a temporary restraining Monday that prevents a bondholder group led by Icahn from taking control of the board of directors of Marvel, said officials representing bondholders and Marvel.
"Today's court ruling means that Marvel and the banks are free to explore all options to protect the company's future," said a Marvel spokesman. He declined further comment.
Bondholders had planned to replace Marvel's current board with their own slate of directors on Tuesday, after foreclosing on 80 million Marvel shares that was collateral for the bonds.

The ruling was just the latest in a battle between Icahn and Ronald Perelman, who bought Marvel in 1988 when it was a relatively small comic book publisher. He expanded it with the purchase of Fleer and SkyBox International trading card companies.
The ruling will likely delay the implementation of a final reorganization plan by sending both sides back into court.
Marvel has contended the bondholder group is fronting for Icahn's interests to "grab control of the company without committing a dollar."
